title: He didn’t wait for you to get it together…
paragraphs:
He didn’t wait for you to get it together…
and that changes everything.
Because most people still don’t understand what happened on that hill.

We think the cross is for the “almost good.”
The “trying hard.”
The “clean enough.”
But Scripture cuts deeper than that.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Not improved.
Not filtered.
Not fixed.

Still lying.
Still hiding.
Still choosing everything but God.

That’s the version of you Jesus saw…
and still chose the cross.
Because we love to believe God helps those who help themselves.

But the Gospel says something far more offensive—
and far more beautiful.
God saves those who cannot save themselves.
That means the cross wasn’t God reacting to your goodness.
It was God invading your brokenness.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable…

It’s not “just a phase.”
Not “just how you are.”
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

Sin separates.
Sin corrupts.
Sin leads to death.
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23

Not just physical—
spiritual separation from a holy God.
That’s what makes the cross necessary.
God didn’t wait for you to climb out of sin.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
Jesus didn’t die as a tragic victim.
Absorbing the wrath you couldn’t escape.
So that grace could reach you without compromising God’s justice.

Blood.
Thorns.
Mockery.
Silence from heaven.
“God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.” — 2 Corinthians 5:21

Your guilt—placed on Christ.
His righteousness—offered to you.
Grace is not permission to stay the same.
“Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase? By no means!” — Romans 6:1–2

If the cross doesn’t change you,
you haven’t truly seen it.

Because when you realize He died for you at your worst,
you stop wanting to live in what nailed Him there.

Not to try harder.
Not to pretend better.
“Repent, then, and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out…” — Acts 3:19

Repent—turn away from sin.
Believe—trust in Jesus alone.

Not your effort.
Not your morality.

Because of what you did last night.
Last week.
Years ago.

Still suffered.
Still chose nails over leaving you lost.
This is not a soft message.

Because the same love that saves you
will transform you.
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation…” — 2 Corinthians 5:17

Stay in what’s killing you…
or surrender to the One who died to save you.
